host_about:
Hi There,

I'm Jonathan, I'm in my mid 40's, sometimes older sometimes younger and I love to travel. 

In terms of a home I love a comfy couch, I love a deep bath and I love full blockout curtains. 

5 things I can't live without?

Books, I love a good book.
Good food. I love sharing a great meal with others.
Long sleep in's on Sundays or any day really.
Water. I love swimming in the ocean or rivers. Lets keep them clean.
Music. Anything from opera to house.

As your host, I will be on call to make your stay as comfortable as possible. If anything goes wrong during your stay, say the washing machine won't start or something, I will have it sorted immediately. I've had guest stay at my place for 3 month and then extend up to 16 months. I've had guests who moved out and then told me if they could stay forever they would be very happy. 

As someone who has travelled a lot with work and stayed in hotels motels and apartments both long and short term, I set out to create a space that was a real home away from home. Somewhere where you can feel safe, warm and cosy and enjoy a good home cooked meal. It was all about atmosphere. A deep bath to relax in, comfy couches to put your feet up on, a big TV to tune out to and stunning view whilst enjoying your breakfast. In winter turn on the gas log fireplace and enjoy a glass of wine. Head out to one of the many great eating establishments on Chapel St, Fitzroy St or take a tram to the city. the tram stop is a 2 minute walk away.

Everyone who has stayed at Charnwood has enjoyed their stay. I'm sure you will too. Great location, affordably priced and in a very convenient but quiet street.

Hi, we are Gus and Feng Feng, and are living as artists raising a young family - Gus is a musician, composer and sound designer who also teaches banjo. Feng Feng is a former dancer with the Chinese Ballet, who has since worked at the Victorian College of the Arts as a choreographer, which is where we met each other when we were both studying there in 2004. In 2018 Feng Feng started studyjng fashion design at RMIT.

We both love good food (cooking and eating!), good films and good music - Feng Feng also makes jewellry, plus has recently developed quite a skill for knitting and sewing for her kids. Her latest project is designing and making cuff-links to sell at markets, re-using old communist badges from the USSR.  In 2018 she started studying fashion design and technology at RMIT.

We are into the nesting phase of our lives, and spend the bulk of our spare time hanging out as a family with our son Wilfred (8) and Emerald (6), which as you can imagine is a fun time of life for them!  But previously we have both done lots of traveling, around Australia as well as to Europe, Asia and America, and loved using the Airbnb website to find cosy and personal spaces that had privacy and a touch of style. We loved the way it allowed us to tap into a city's culture on a more personal level. Over the summer of 2013/14 we decided to build an extension on to our house so Feng Feng's parents had a place to stay when they visited from China. The at the start of 2016 we branched out and acquired an apartment in the city of Melbourne to add to our Airbnb portfolio. We selected one that we thought had the best possible location - slap bang in the middle of town. It has been great to host people in such a fantastic location and help them to discover the heart of the city.

We both love living in Brunswick - there's so much interesting stuff going on in the community, lots of venues, cafes, gourmet food trucks, street art, galleries, theatre and shops, it really is the centre of Melbourne's creative heart. We'd love you to come and stay with us, do come and visit!

host_about:
(Click on my logo above to see more than 20 other StayCentral listings).

I started StayCentral Melbourne Corporate Apartments with one apartment, and now manage multiple properties in many different locations in inner Melbourne.

Like many of my guests, I love to travel; both overseas to places like the Mulu Caves in Borneo, ancient cities (in many old countries), Antarctica & Alaska, Patagonia, and colourful markets in amazing places like Pha Long in Vietnam, Jaisalmer in India, Tozeur in Tunisia & La Paz in Bolivia. I also love short domestic trips for weekends away just to relax. 

It means I get to be on the other side of the counter, and experience how other people look after their guests: and I take their good ideas back with me. 

I even worked as a part-time tourist guide in Melbourne for a couple of years when I arrived here, and really enjoyed the interactions with the tourists off the huge cruise liners that appear in Melbourne each spring and summer. I have tried to extend this experience into my accommodation business here in Melbourne, where I really love assisting people with their stays. You only need to read some of the 1,000 plus reviews on Airbnb, Trip Advisor, Goo gle, and on my own StayCentral Melbourne Corporate Apartments website to realise how much our guests enjoy our apartments, and the way we look after them. 

I do love living in Melbourne. It enjoys a unique place in Australia. It is often described as the cultural, business, shopping and sporting capital of the country. The restaurants and cafes in Melbourne are amongst the best in the world. I love living in an urban village amongst these, and all the other everyday shops; and jumping on a tram and avoiding the hassles of traffic. It is a city of great opportunity, experiences, events and lifestyle that can be enjoyed by locals and visitors alike; and I really enjoy facilitating our guests' stays here.

I do hope I have the opportunity to help you get to know Melbourne and grow to love it as I have. If you have any questions about StayCentral Melbourne Corporate Apartments, please feel free to call me on (Phone number hidden by Airbnb) during business hours, and I will do my best to help you.

Park Street is a beautiful leafy road in the shade of ancient English elm trees. Although 100 meters from thriving Fitzroy Street, Park Street is remarkably quiet and the atmosphere is very residential.
Supermarket, dry cleaning laundry, 24 hour convenience store, bottle shop all within just a few minutes walk.
If you like walking or running, Albert Park is 300 meters away, or you can walk or run along the foreshore to Port Melbourne in one direction, or the St Kilda promenade in the other.
If you have kids, the Famous Luna Park is a short stroll, as is Acland Street with it's bustling street life and some of Melbourne's best cafes, restaurants and pastry shops.
If you love animals, St Kilda has its own Penguin Colony which appears at dusk each night, alongside the St Kilda Pier.
host_about:
Hi there! We are Marco & Paul! 

We are really helpful and resourceful guys. We eat out a lot and are real foodies. We love Melbourne and St Kilda in particular, and have lived here for years so know all it's fun places to go!

Our style of traveling is being able to immerse ourselves in local culture! We love getting to see the way the locals live, We are not really attracted to doing the "touristy" sort of things but rather getting to know someone for who they are and not just for what they are stereotyped as! We love to try things out of the norm and are always seeking out our next adventure and making friends all along the way!

Our son Louis lives in Portland, Maine, USA where he works for the Boston Celtics basketball team as Player Manager of their second team the Maine Celtics.  He attended university in Boston, USA and represented Australia in rowing as a coxswain. 

On weekends, given a chance, we will visit a beach side holiday apartment with stunning sea views in Torquay. Torquay is just over an hour’s drive from Melbourne. We have travelled to Europe, the Middle East, South East Asia and the USA where we have enjoyed Airbnb hospitality in England, France, Italy, Spain, Bulgaria, Croatia, Turkey, Netherlands, Denmark, Sweden and the United States. With a family of designers I am always working on some property development or creative project for myself,  family and friends.

I like to catch a movie or show and visit galleries and believing that you should “be a tourist in your own town” try get out and about to something interesting either near or far. 

I look forward to sharing the great properties which I manage and my local experience with my guests.

Your host, 

Gary Copolov.

Hello, we are Ken and Mark.  We live in Melbourne Australia.  Mark works in IT and Ken is a Chiropractor.  We love to travel and in the past few years have been on trips to Europe, Middle East, US, Asia and South America.  We love cruising because it's an easy way to see cities and places of the world without having to see the inside of an airport or lug a suitcase.  In 2013 we did a Transatlantic cruise from Rome to Fort Lauderdale and another from Buenos Aires to Santiago Chile.  Enjoying that so much we did another Transatlantic from Barcelona to Buenos Aires in 2018.  When on land we like to stay at b&b's, homestays or private apartments. Our favourite cities and places include Rome, Berlin, Jordan (you have to go to Petra and Jarash), Bangkok, Cambodia (try the train trip from Bangkok to Cambodia), Barcelona, Peru (yes, another must is Machu Picchu as is the Titicaca train), Rio, La Paz and Santiago.  Egypt also makes the list being a sensory overload  of history and culture every minute of the day.

Our bucket list includes the Galapagos Islands, a Baltic cruise and lots more of Europe.  We also want to see more of the USA.   Whilst we think we've done a lot of the US we've only just scratched the surface.  Our bucket list includes driving the winnebago from West to East coast (with lots of zig zagging along the way).   

Ken is an avid cook and Mark an avid Collingwood (AFL) supporter.  Don't hold that against him.  We're long time Melbourne locals.  Both born in Victoria we've lived Melbourne inner city, South, East and on the Mornington Peninsula.  We've also lived in various cities around Australia (Sydney, Brisbane, Perth, Mildura, Warnambool, Bright and Darwin) and have been lucky enough to experience life living overseas in New Zealand and the USA.

Botanical research, wildlife rescue & conservation, outback bush travel, and Airedale Rescue work, together with running our B&B, still enables us to cherish the special moments of each day when the wildlife of Wombat Bend and the light across the billabong capture and hold our attention, and we become part of the landscape that we have created.  We welcome all who share such a vision.  I'd say our life philosophy is that everyone can make a difference ~ for the better.  

Though we've been hosting guests here at Wombat Bend for years, we're thrilled to now offer this unique retreat through Airbnb.  Recent guests captured the spirit of the space when they wrote to us afterwards.....

 'We had a wonderful stay at The Burrow.  We felt our shoulders just drop when we arrived...  The cacophony of frogs' songs at night, perfect starry skies, rolling out of bed late to have coffee on the veranda with the birds and the billabong... plus a perfect homebase for all that the area has to offer.  Thank you for hosting us and our children - we can see how budding naturalists are inspired by your space and your passion! ‘

And from the heart ..... "Thanks for such an amazing getaway.  From the second we walked in, we instantly felt relaxed.  Your hospitality and kindness is amazing, and accompanied by such a beautiful tranquil cottage, makes for perfection. We can't wait to visit again!"

It doesn't get any nicer than that, does it?

host_about:
Hello World, I'm sharing my local knowledge with the world... one guest at a time.

I have traveled quite extensively every 2-3 years for usually 3-4 months at a time. The first time I traveled Overseas alone was when I was 16, to the US and Canada.  I lived in the UK for 2 1/2 years and again for 3 months a few years ago and most of my traveling has been backpacking and using other sharing economy websites, staying on couches and letting out my couch.  I used AirBnB during my 3 week trip to New Zealand in 2013 and thought this is perfect for me living right in the heart of the city and working in Tourism and Events I can share my local knowledge with the world... one guest at a time.

I work in Events Management and have worked on such exciting events as the London Olympics 2012, The Commonwealth Games, The Australian Open and the Tim Burton Exhibition Opening at ACMI.

I love horse riding, travel, theatre, comedy shows, live bands and seeing and experiencing what the world has to offer.  I have traveled extensively but I am in love with Melbourne and its many faces.

I am a frugal traveler and love to share my tips and there is a lot to see and do in Melbourne that is free.  I have worked in the Tourism Industry so I know this place pretty well and living in the city well, it gives life a completely different flavour, I love it.

Why AirBnB?
Simple as a keen traveler and loving my city I want to share it.  I live in a central location and I have had many friends across the world stay, some whom I have met on my travels, some who became friends after they stayed.

AirBnB will help me stay in my apartment, living in the city can be quite expensive so by utilsing AirBnB I can continue to live in the city I love.

AirBnB has helped me renovate upstairs, removing my carpet and replacing with floorboards.  Installing a custom blind of Melbourne's art centre and skyline, and most recently it contributed to an new kitchen! How awesome is that!

Next goal your stay is contributing to:  New Carpet in the downstairs area its well loved by me, cats and guests so isnt perfect.

host_about:
I was born in Melbourne, and know the attraction of Melbourne is very much about its lifestyle. While it’s still got its “Hustle & Bustle” the magic about Melbourne is how it balances this hectic activity with the arts, sports and entertaining. Melbournian’s have passion for living life and that’s a major element towards Melbourne being voted as one of the world’s most liveable and friendliest cities (EIU's Global Liveability Ranking)

I have spent most of my life on the Mornington Peninsula (one hour south of Melbourne). I work in Melbourne’s CBD and have now also moved into the city to live. I’m an avid traveler, but with so many destinations still explore both in Australia and overseas. 
My greatest memories of traveling are often the people you meet and the experiences that are not found on the main tourist trail. I always love talking to a local character getting that special place to visit or café to dine (usually a cousin’s cafe). 
I have now come to a stage in my life I’d like to share some of Melbourne’s special places with others. These are not only my places of interest but also those hidden secrets that previous guests have found and have been excited to share with us.

I like to think “Abode 316 & 317” are special!  They are less than a year old and designed to be functional, yet have a touch of sophistication. They are fully optioned for the traveler and create that home away from home a hotel just can’t offer. 
Accommodation can often make or break a holiday, but I know the accommodation and hospitality my apartments will add to your Melbourne experience.
Rob

Shortly after the turn of the 20th century, St Kilda served a similar function for Melburnians as did Coney Island to the residents of New York City and its history draws an interesting parallel. I look forward to meeting you.

Maria

host_about:
We are a nurse (Angus) and a Human Resource professional (Lana) and we LOVE to travel, spend time with friends, cycle, crochet and read. Although Angus wanted to make sure that it's me that likes crocheting! 

The five things I can't live without are: chocolate, coffee, animals (specifically my sausage dog Coco and our giant cat called Ted), friends and family!

AS A TRAVELLER(Lana)
In 2013 I went to France, Italy, Serbia, Croatia and Vietnam with a friend where we backpacked and AirBnB'd around, went to a music festival and hired a car to drive around.
In 2014 I went to New York on my own for a couple of weeks for a music festival, stayed at a hostel.
In 2015, I took my parents on a 5 week European extravaganza through France, Italy and Greece. We hired a car and took our time meandering through and staying exclusively w AirBnB. 
In 2016, I think I stayed in Australia, but... I met Angus!
2017 was action packed, we went to NZ to be the 'best lady' army friends wedding. 
In 2017 I went to Italy, Montenegro and Serbia for my 35th birthday celebrations. I travelled with my two friends and Angus. Staying at AirBnB places of course! 

Style: I treat others as I like to be treated, and that includes belongings and their properties. I am respectful and if I'm going to be partying, it will be outside! I am an extroverted, social person who loves getting out and about.

AS A HOST
I joined AirBnB as a host in July 2015 when I was travelling around and not at home for lengthy periods. So I put up my one bedroom apartment up on Airbnb which gave me a piece of mind to ensure that someone will be in there and I absolutely love my apartment and want everyone else to as well!

Since then, in early 2019 we bought our townhouse in Abbotsford. It needed some TLC so we spent a few months (read: every spare waking moment) renovating on our home ready for us to move in. However we're house sitting until November in Moonee Ponds which is about 8km from our new home.

We have spent a lot of time renovating it but you will find me constantly shuffling things around. I am definitely a home body when I'm at home and love being surrounded by pretty, tidy clean areas. 

I like to think about what things are important to me when I am looking at places on AirBnB and make sure I have those ready!

Favourite Destination: Italy 
Book: The Girl with all the Gifts, The Time Traveller's Wife
Movies: Some Like it Hot, Ace Ventura, Crazy Stupid Love
Music: Anything I can dance to!
Food: Anything sweet, or salty, or crunchy, or sour.... okay, everything!

Motto: it is what it is.

A former dairy farm that originally sat on 150 acres that their neighbours owned. In 1977 it was divided into three, 50 acre lots and Brian and Lynette bought the middle lot which had 2 creeks and a dam. With no means to access the back paddocks they had to create the drive and 2 creek crossings, this is one highlight many guests can enjoy as the 1km long winding drive provides stunning views and and exciting entry into the property.

Lynette started planning and commenced work on the garden before the house was built. 

In 1990 they started the building of the main house. Lynette was the designer and Brian the builder.

Brian together with Melissa, his daughter-in-law, runs the property and is caretaker for Lynette’s final resting place.

With no means to access the back paddocks they had to create the drive and 2 creek crossings, this is one highlight many guests can enjoy as the 1km long winding drive provides stunning views and and exciting entry into the property.

host_about:
YOUR HOST: GARY COPOLOV 

Hello, my name is Gary and I live in Middle Park, Melbourne. I currently manage sixteen short to long term accommodation properties in Middle Park (6), Albert Park (3), South Melbourne (4), Port Melbourne (1), North Carlton (1), Torquay (1). Middle Park, Albert Park, South Melbourne and Port Melbourne. These are arguably some of Melbourne’s best inner city suburbs. I believe I am fortunate to live and manage properties in the area and meet and host wonderful guests. 

My Airbnb hosting journey started when my wife, Jo and I bought Florence Court in Nimmo Street, Middle Park in 2015. It is a heritage listed, mid 30's Art Deco apartment block in where I now offer four  fantastic short term accommodation apartments. I now operate sixteen brilliant short to long term accommodation properties in the area ranging from apartments to houses and from one to four bedrooms. They are all stunning and fitted out to the very highest standard. 

As an Airbnb Superhost I offer my guests a concierge like service. I am an unashamed ambassador for the area where I have lived for over 30 years. Just tell me your interests and I will offer my recommendations. 

Each property has a copy of "Adventures" which provides details my recommended local To Do's and the very best of nearby dining pleasures. There are many recommendations for guests of all ages. 

Jo and I met playing tennis at Kooyong Lawn Tennis Club and were married in Paris just over 28 years ago. Jo is a part time teacher at the local primary school where she is a special education reading teacher. She has a real passion for books, real estate and interior design. A typical week will see her at a local café with friends, walking our dog in the nearby park, seeing a movie, attending her book club or a yoga class. 

We have two children. Natasha (Tash) an Architecture - Design graduate working in the construction industry. When she is not out socialising or globetrotting she may occasionally walk our friendly Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever called Hudson. We love pets and welcome them at all properties. 

Our son Louis lives in Portland, Maine, USA where he works for the Boston Celtics basketball team as Player Manager of their second team the Maine Celtics.  He attended university in Boston, USA and represented Australia in rowing as a coxswain. 

On weekends, given a chance, we will visit a beach side holiday apartment with stunning sea views in Torquay. Torquay is just over an hour’s drive from Melbourne. It is Victoria's surf capital and the gateway to the famous Great Ocean Road. In Torquay, we enjoy walks, great local food, wine, the many surf beaches and the company of friends. The apartment is available for stays on Airbnb. (Sleeps 8). 

We have travelled to Europe, the Middle East, South East Asia and the USA where we have enjoyed Airbnb hospitality in England, France, Italy, Spain, Bulgaria, Croatia, Turkey, Netherlands, Denmark, Sweden and the United States. I wish to share the same pleasure and the excitement of travel with my guests. 

I am a self-employed Marketing Consultant whose consultancy, Gold Medal Marketing develops and implements winning business development programs for businesses in various industries. I have written and delivered a number of business development programs. 

I am the honorary Chairman of the Australian Patients Association (APA) which advocates, educates and supports Australian patients. The APA strives to be the voice of and for Australian patients. 

I regularly attend a local gym for regular workouts which I would be pleased to introduce to my guests. 

On weekends in Winter I watch St. Kilda, an Australian Rules Football Club as a long standing and sadly long suffering club member.

With a family of designers I am always working on some property development or creative project for myself,  family and friends.

I like to catch a movie or show and visit galleries and believing that you should “be a tourist in your own town” try get out and about to something interesting either near or far. 

I look forward to sharing the great properties which I manage and my local experience with my guests. 

I am available to ensure that you have a great stay. 

Your host, 

Gary Copolov.

host_about:
I was born in Melbourne, and know the attraction of Melbourne is very much about its lifestyle. While it’s still got its “Hustle & Bustle” the magic about Melbourne is how it balances this hectic activity with the arts, sports and entertaining. Melbournian’s have passion for living life and that’s a major element towards Melbourne being voted as one of the world’s most liveable and friendliest cities (EIU's Global Liveability Ranking)

My greatest memories of traveling are often the people you meet and the experiences that are not found on the main tourist trail. I always love talking to a local character getting that special place to visit or café to dine (usually a cousin’s cafe). 
I have now come to a stage in my life I’d like to share some of Melbourne’s special places with others. These are not only my places of interest but also those hidden secrets that previous guests have found and have been excited to share with us.

I like to think “Abode 316 & 317” are special!  They are less than a year old and designed to be functional, yet have a touch of sophistication. They are fully optioned for the traveler and create that home away from home a hotel just can’t offer. 
Accommodation can often make or break a holiday, but I know the accommodation and hospitality my apartments will add to your Melbourne experience.
Rob

neighborhood_overview:
Warburton is a quiet little town in the end pocket of the Yarra Valley. A hamlet surrounded by tall mountains with a fresh water river running through it. It also happens to be in one of Australia (and the world's) best wine regions!

This quaint town sits at the end of the dividing range in Victoria, influenced by the Bass Strait weather patterns; it is lush year round with abundant wildlife and dense flora.

There's plenty to do:

Bushwalking - by the river, La La Falls, Mt Donna Buang - just to name a few.

Bike riding - ride all or part of the 40km historic Lilydale- Warburton rail trail. Mountain bike tracks are great to ride (bikes are available for hire in the street at the Cog Cafe).

River - swim, kayak or tube in the fresh water river in summer.

Winter - fun in the snow in winter, tobogganing.

Hello, my name is Gary and I live in Middle Park, Melbourne. I currently manage sixteen short to long term accommodation properties in Middle Park (6), Albert Park (3), South Melbourne (4), Port Melbourne (1), North Carlton (1), Torquay (1). Jo is a part time teacher at the local primary school where she is a special education reading teacher. She has a real passion for books, real estate and interior design. A typical week will see her at a local café with friends, walking our dog in the nearby park, seeing a movie, attending her book club or a yoga class. 

We have two children. Natasha (Tash) an Architecture - Design graduate working in the construction industry. When she is not out socialising or globetrotting she may occasionally walk our friendly Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever called Hudson. We love pets and welcome them at all properties. 

Our son Louis lives in Portland, Maine, USA where he works for the Boston Celtics basketball team as Player Manager of their second team the Maine Celtics.  He attended university in Boston, USA and represented Australia in rowing as a coxswain. 

On weekends, given a chance, we will visit a beach side holiday apartment with stunning sea views in Torquay. Torquay is just over an hour’s drive from Melbourne. On weekends in Winter I watch St. Kilda, an Australian Rules Football Club as a long standing and sadly long suffering club member.

With a family of designers I am always working on some property development or creative project for myself,  family and friends.

I am available to ensure that you have a great stay. 

Your host, 

Gary Copolov.

name: Double Room, Shared Bathroom
description:
Built in 1886 and tastefully restored, Hotel Claremont Guesthouse gives you the best of both worlds - old charm-world located in vibrant South Yarra, and fantastic value for money. We offer private double rooms with ample spotlessly clean shared bathroom facilities. Fan, heating, all linen included.
Unlimited WiFi access included.
Our location is perfect - 100 metres from South Yarra Train Station, 150 metres from Chapel St. There's trams, shops, cafes, and bars at our door.

The space
Double rooms have one double bed with linen and towels included, WiFi access, a desk, TV, fan and heater. Bathrooms are shared, with several clean, modern bathrooms at the end of every corridor. Rooms are located on the first and second floors, with access via our grand staircase. Late arrival available, just let us know.

Guest access
All bathrooms are shared. There are 25 individually lockable, modern bathrooms each with one shower and one toilet.
neighborhood_overview:
South Yarra - a Melbourne location like no other! So close to the CBD, yet a personality of its own.
Award-winning restaurants line elegant streets and beckon both local and visitor.
Rich multicultural banquets of the world's great cuisines. Chinese, Greek, Italian, French, South East Asian, Vietnamese, Middle Eastern are only a few steps away from the Hotel Claremont. Join the people of Melbourne as they love to dine al fresco and can be found any time, day or night, along any of the many cafes spilling onto pavements.
From luxurious five-star dining and bustling fashionable bistros to casual and relaxed cafes, all tastes and budgets are covered.
You can uncork world class wines in your choice of restaurant, bar and cafe. And when you've eaten your fill, it's time to ...
Shop til you drop! From Haute Couture to a Bargain Lovers paradise, it's all here.
When you've had enough, enjoy one of the local high-end spas for a beauty treatment or relaxing massage

host_about:
I live in Melbourne and the majority of my career has been in the creative industries, moving to Melbourne from London where I produced theatre and ran festivals. I now work in a really interesting role in board leadership development, which I love. In my free time I exercise, binge watch great drama, read, attend arts events, spend time in nature, hike, swim and love spending time with friends. 

 I have always loved to travel and have done so all my life. I regularly travel interstate for work and overseas, hence the entire apartment is available on occasions and on a separate listing, titled "Luxury Apartment Opposite St Kilda Beach and Pier". 

I enjoy camping as much as quirky luxury as I became fed up with the over emphasis on having to have the very best of everything at the expense of the environment and a living wage! 

I love using Airbnb as its a great way to stay in amazingly beautiful and eclectic places, meeting locals and gaining insights into what one should see and do while visiting their turf.  I have used Airbnb in Sydney, Hobart, Brisbane, London, Los Angeles, California & Vancouver when visiting friends and family. I love chilling out in a homely environment, visiting local markets & cooking with great ingredients rather than eating out all the time. I am interested in a culture of exchange and sharing. I dislike waste and entitlement. I have been able to develop so many ideas and projects with the skills, expertise & open attitudes of Helpxers & Woofers I have worked with over the years. I regularly host and participate in Clothes & Skills Swaps. All of these schemes have enriched my life and brought me into contact with some amazing people from all over the world.

Flemington is located between the Maribyrnong River and the Moonee Ponds Creek and includes the locality of Newmarket, in which the main commercial area Racecourse Road is located. The Melbourne Cup Thoroughbred horse race has been held at Flemington Racecourse since 1861.

A backpacker for many years, I now prefer a little more comfort, exercise, meditation and 3 meals a day instead of 1 meal and copious beer - how times change with age!

I want guests to enjoy their time visiting Melbourne, and know that they have a quiet, clean space to come home to and rest.

My travels have taken me across Europe, Scandinavia, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Singapore, Israel, Egypt, Jordan, India, Nepal, Mexico and USA. 

As a host I like to meet my guests if we can make the time. I'm available by phone and am responsive to texts (although not in the middle of the night)! I'm not intrusive, but enjoy meeting travellers from around the world especially when they're staying in my home. As a guest I'm also happy to meet the host, and have contact as required. Friendships form in unlikely places and Air BnB was set up to build connections with others based on trust and goodwill, as such my place is not a hotel, it's my home and I hope the guests that I attract will treat it with respect and not abuse my hospitality. 

Life motto: Jump and the net will appear - don't know who said this, but I think it's a good one and it works most times.

host_about:
“Travel is little beds and cramped bathrooms.
It’s old television sets and slow Internet connections.
Travel is extraordinary conversations with ordinary people.
It’s waiters, gas station attendants, and housekeepers becoming the most interesting people in the world.
It’s churches that are compelling enough to enter.
It’s McDonald’s being a luxury.
It’s the realization that you may have been born in the wrong country.
Travel is a smile that leads to a conversation in broken English.
It’s the epiphany that pretty girls smile the same way all over the world.
Travel is tipping 10% and being embraced for it.
Travel is the same white T-shirt again tomorrow.
Travel is flowing in the back of a bus with giggly strangers.

I'm a semi retired former co-owner of a video production company and until further notice, fit, sane and without significant personality disorders.  To date I've travelled mostly in Asia and particularly in Thailand but I have a son and daughter who work in Cambodia, which I visit from time to time as well.   Most recently though, I've spent some time in Europe.  Travel is in my blood and so long as I can keep putting one foot in front of the other, I'll keep it up.  
I've sampled all sorts of accommodation but prefer light and airy places with a bit of room, some temperature control, Wi Fi connection, a bit of outside space and proximity to public transport.  
With few exceptions, whatever it happens to be, I love places with a vibrant culture, especially when it's there to be enjoyed on the street.  I also like being close to water, particularly when it's lapping up on a beach and I'm a big fan of locations with their own distinctive food - and where grapevines flourish - wine as well.  
Books?  All sorts but I particularly like biographies, engrossingly well written novels and histories and descriptions of places I've never been to and may never visit.  Movies? once or twice a week, the most recent one that really impressed was 'Three Billboards...'. 
As a guest who's also a home owner, I treat my host's house or apartment as if it were my own, so I keep it clean and tidy and respect the furniture and fittings: as a host, I expect the same from my guests. Aside from that I'm pretty easy going and like meeting people from all walks of life and hearing about whatever aspects of their lives they choose to share with me.

name: Peaceful pad in St Kilda East.
description:
I love my charming two-bedroom apartment. It offers guests an extremely comfortable base to explore Chapel Street, St Kilda and beyond. Five minute walk to trams, and another five to Windsor train station, you can be to the CBD in twenty minutes. Alma Park is just around the corner. Fifteen minutes stroll to the south, bohemian Carlisle Street offers a choice of cafes, restaurants and organic supermarkets. *Please read house rules prior to booking.

The space
My apartment is clutter free and has lots of character.

**LIVING ROOM: A great place to relax, with a luxurious leather sofa and 1960's style armchairs that are perfect for lounging around and chatting. A large flat screen TV mounted on an exposed brick wall brings an industrial edge, and floor to ceiling curtains create a sense of style and elegance. Reverse-cycle air conditioning keeps things at the optimum temperature.

**KITCHEN: This light-filled fully-equipped (except dishwasher)
neighborhood_overview:
I love this neighbourhood. It’s within walking distance of the Windsor end of Chapel Street, which has tonnes of exciting bars and restaurants. My favourites are Hawker Hall, Marmara and Hooked. There’s also a branch of Messina for delicious gelatos.

Alma Park, just around the corner from my place, has barbecues and picnic areas. If you feel like chilling out in classic surroundings, grab a choc top and catch a screening at the Astor Cinema. There’s no shortage of great coffee places but my go to is Batch on Carlisle Street.

There’s a newly renovated Fitness First with indoor swimming pool five minutes walk away and if you like organic food, head to Aunt Maggie’s Organic Supermarket on Carlisle Street, Balaclava. If you want to treat yourself head to St Kilda Sea Baths and enjoy a salt water pool with super views of Port Phillip.
host_about: I'm a friendly, easygoing Irish man with a keen mind and a great sense of humour. I work as an actor, writer and producer. I have a very full life. I love great food and good company. I'm a big sports fan and I like to stay active. I have traveled a lot, so I know what makes a good host - someone who can be helpful and informative, without interfering. I'm happy to share my knowledge of Melbourne and the local area. If there's a question I can't answer, I'll know someone who can. I'm happy to welcome you to my home and I will do my best to make your stay a memorable and enjoyable one.

Hi I'm John.

During the week I work in my recording studio and am busy writing and producing music, as well as remixing and producing other artists. I also direct videoclips.
If you're interested in synthpop/electronic music then do a search for "Parralox".

As such, I usually travel overseas at least 3 times a year. Travel is one of the best things in the world (long haul flights, not so much!)

I'm a MAJOR Science Fiction fan. Favourite authors are Larry Niven, Arthur C Clarke and Frank Herbert. Favourite directors are David Lynch & Stanley Kubrick.

I'm very passionate about Animal Rights. Animal cruelty is my biggest hate. I donate monthly to The Lost Dogs Home.
I have a dog called Jack that I treat like absolute gold. You’ll get to meet him when I check you in!
 With so much suffering on this planet I figure that if I can give one animal a perfect life then I'm doing something good.

host_about:
Hi I'm John.

During the week I work in my recording studio and am busy writing and producing music, as well as remixing and producing other artists. I also direct videoclips.
If you're interested in synthpop/electronic music then do a search for "Parralox".

As such, I usually travel overseas at least 3 times a year. Travel is one of the best things in the world (long haul flights, not so much!)

On the weekends I work as a registered Nurse (Permanent Night Shifts!) at a major Melbourne City Hospital.

I also dabble in property investment and my current property portfolio is 7 properties so far. You'll find some of them listed here on AirBNB from time to time!

I'm a MAJOR Science Fiction fan. Favourite authors are Larry Niven, Arthur C Clarke and Frank Herbert. Favourite directors are David Lynch & Stanley Kubrick.

I'm very passionate about Animal Rights. Animal cruelty is my biggest hate. I donate monthly to The Lost Dogs Home.
I have a dog called Jack that I treat like absolute gold. You’ll get to meet him when I check you in!
 With so much suffering on this planet I figure that if I can give one animal a perfect life then I'm doing something good.

neighborhood_overview:
Travelling along the dirt road to my home, the sun peeps through the trees, the road has no traffic so the.wild residents are abundant. Kangaroos, wombats, bird life galore are to be seen. Stars at night are clear and the odd falling star is seen. Deer come and drink from the dam while the sound of kookaburras settling in for the night. Echidnas and the odd king parrot show up on your doorstep all the while sheep, goat and pony are wondering the paddock.

host_about:
Hey there you curious creatures! Time to share a little about ourselves. Mike was born and raised in New Zealand and I have a Greek background but am from a small country town in Victoria. We Travel Not To Escape Life, But For Life Not To Escape Us.

See you very soon!

(Click on my logo above to see more than 20 other StayCentral listings).

I started StayCentral Melbourne Corporate Apartments with one apartment, and now manage multiple properties in many different locations in inner Melbourne.

Like many of my guests, I love to travel; both overseas to places like the Mulu Caves in Borneo, ancient cities (in many old countries), Antarctica & Alaska, Patagonia, and colourful markets in amazing places like Pha Long in Vietnam, Jaisalmer in India, Tozeur in Tunisia & La Paz in Bolivia. I also love short domestic trips for weekends away just to relax. 

It means I get to be on the other side of the counter, and experience how other people look after their guests: and I take their good ideas back with me. 

I even worked as a part-time tourist guide in Melbourne for a couple of years when I arrived here, and really enjoyed the interactions with the tourists off the huge cruise liners that appear in Melbourne each spring and summer. I have tried to extend this experience into my accommodation business here in Melbourne, where I really love assisting people with their stays. You only need to read some of the 1,000 plus reviews on Airbnb, Trip Advisor, Goo gle, and on my own StayCentral Melbourne Corporate Apartments website to realise how much our guests enjoy our apartments, and the way we look after them. 

I do love living in Melbourne. It enjoys a unique place in Australia. It is often described as the cultural, business, shopping and sporting capital of the country. The restaurants and cafes in Melbourne are amongst the best in the world. I love living in an urban village amongst these, and all the other everyday shops; and jumping on a tram and avoiding the hassles of traffic. It is a city of great opportunity, experiences, events and lifestyle that can be enjoyed by locals and visitors alike; and I really enjoy facilitating our guests' stays here.

I do hope I have the opportunity to help you get to know Melbourne and grow to love it as I have. If you have any questions about StayCentral Melbourne Corporate Apartments, please feel free to call me on (Phone number hidden by Airbnb) during business hours, and I will do my best to help you.

host_about:
Hi, my name is Dawei, I started doing Airbnb September 2015. 

I'm a 20 years old undergraduate student currently studying commercial law. I like to watch movies and play video games. Sometimes I could spend my whole day in my room just play games. I thought that there isn't many things to do outside and I thought the World was a boring place. When I'm not playing games, I would read news on the internet just to catch up with the rest of the world. That's how I knew Airbnb. 

My father talked about doing short-term renting. He has got a few new apartments that our relatives bought which needs to be rented out. I told him about Airbnb and he thought we could really make it work. So I asked my best friend if he is interested to be my partner for this, and he said yes. We started almost immediately, planning, buying furniture to started taking guests in just two weeks. 

Then it really changed me.

I met with travelers around the world. Everybody was so polite and friendly.  When I talk to them I can feel the excitement and happiness. It's totally different compared to what I thought people are like. Maybe because this communicate is great, I don't know.  Then I  thought "I want to be people like my guests". I want people around me to feel life is great and there are a lot to look forward to. The guests really gave me a lot of motivation towards my work and my life. Here I have to thank you all.

After one month, the revenue was great, however, take away the interests and loans, all kinds of fees and salary for my partner, there are really not much left for me. But I think that's enough, I'm still a student, I have to spend time on study and don't have many things to spend money on anyway, being able to save money for a holiday with my girlfriend every few months is perfect for me. 

After all these experience, I felt it really changed my life and how I view the world. Doesn't matter if I fail or succeed it's going to affect the rest of my life in a very positive way, that's something really valuable to me.

Brett grew up in a sleepy idyllic town on the beach called Moonta in South Australia, and I am originally from beautiful Vancouver, Canada.

We love travelling and after having stayed in many hotel rooms and apartments over the years, we definitely know what we look for when staying away from home, and we have tried our best to make our homes as comfortable, well-stocked and convenient for guests as possible. If there’s one word that describes St Kilda, it’s eclectic. Beginning life as a glittering seaside resort, it evolved into the gritty epicentre of Melbourne’s bohemian scene. These days it is home to trendy cafés, bustling markets, a rowdy nightlife and backpackers aplenty.

St Kilda’s population is as eclectic as the suburb itself. A veritable mecca for backpackers, travellers can’t get enough of the area’s beachside charm and cheap and cheery drinking dens.

We're Klaudia (Sanctuary Artist), Jonathan (The Oracle), Maria (Fairy Godmother) and Tony (Maker of Worlds), a multi-cultural family all living in Melbourne. We're all different in many ways, but we all share one thing in common: a passion for unique and magical experiences. 

We have long since wished there were easy ways to escape our busy city lives and retreat into a magical, beautiful and peaceful space that feels like another world. This idea eventually evolved into a mission to build with our own hands Melbourne's very own magical sanctuaries and to share it with the rest of the world.

We love imagining what we could create, to build, and to share them with the world through hosting. We constantly think about how to make our creations bring an even greater sense of joy and wonder, and not about how much it'll cost us. We're genuinely excited and happy to host each new guest, to hear about what they love about our creations, and what we could do to make it even better.

We have built and opened our first three installments of Melbourne's hidden sanctuary, which we lovingly refer to as "Heaven & Earth", "Little world of Ice & Snow" and "Mini Renaissance". We have plans to make it even better, as well as other ideas for other worlds we want to try building for our next installments.

Hi from Bronnie and Neil ;-)

You wouldn't call us 'party animals', but we do like socialising and meeting people.  We enjoy a wide variety of interests, love the movies, eating out, popping down to the beach or river, and enjoying the many exciting sporting events and festivals that Melbourne and regional Victoria has to offer.
Our motto is "strangers are friends you haven't met yet!"

Best regards
Bronnie and Neil

Hi from Bronnie and Neil ;-)
We love being airbnb hosts and sharing our homes and our beautiful city with others.
We have been airbnb hosts since 2013 and during that time we have met thousands of amazing and wonderful people from all around the world and Australia.

On a personal note, we're pretty easy going, and love getting out and about exploring different places. We are both keen travellers and have done our fair share of it in Australia and overseas - whether backpacking, camping, or an occasional splurge on 5-star resorts! You wouldn't call us 'party animals', but we do like socialising and meeting people.  We enjoy a wide variety of interests, love the movies, eating out, popping down to the beach or river, and enjoying the many exciting sporting events and festivals that Melbourne and regional Victoria has to offer.
Our motto is "strangers are friends you haven't met yet!"
Wishing you happy travels and looking forward to meeting you soon :-)

Best regards
Bronnie and Neil

I started StayCentral Melbourne Corporate Apartments with one apartment, and now manage multiple properties in many different locations in inner Melbourne.

Like many of my guests, I love to travel; both overseas to places like the Mulu Caves in Borneo, ancient cities (in many old countries), Antarctica & Alaska, Patagonia, and colourful markets in amazing places like Pha Long in Vietnam, Jaisalmer in India, Tozeur in Tunisia & La Paz in Bolivia. I also love short domestic trips for weekends away just to relax. 

It means I get to be on the other side of the counter, and experience how other people look after their guests: and I take their good ideas back with me. 

I even worked as a part-time tourist guide in Melbourne for a couple of years when I arrived here, and really enjoyed the interactions with the tourists off the huge cruise liners that appear in Melbourne each spring and summer. I have tried to extend this experience into my accommodation business here in Melbourne, where I really love assisting people with their stays. host_about:
We proudly offer you a boutique selection of Rooms, Suites, Apartments and Cottages (many with water views) in beautiful, historic, Williamstown.

Rooms & Suites
Our lovely old home is just one door from the water, boat marina and restaurants and has been tastefully renovated and decorated so that every room has ensuites (some with spas) and most of the rooms also have gas log fires. One of the rooms has its own private lounge and balcony but other guests can enjoy the shared lounge room with fire and bay window.  

Apartments & Cottages
The apartments and cottages that we offer are dotted around Williamstown and most are an easy walk to the restaurants, yacht-clubs and shops. They vary from 1-4 bedrooms and 1-3 bathrooms. (One apartment even has a 4th toilet). 

We are not just offering a spare room in our house. This is our business and we are a dedicated team working to ensure that your stay is comfortable.  We are very careful about the apartments and cottages that we choose to take on and have refused many from owners wanting us to manage them.

Having said that, Williamstown is the oldest suburb in Melbourne and therefore some of the classic older apartments have décor such as shower over the bath. Whilst I would normally say no to venues like this, there are two apartments that have this but their other qualities so far outweigh that one negative and I quietly chip away at the owners in order for that to be changed.  I mention this because we want you to let us know if you have mobility issues so that we can suggest other venues for you. 

Other than beds (which are purchased to order and very comfortable!!), I love to buy antique and pre-loved furniture to fit certain venues and I have them restored using classic and sometimes quirky fabrics so you will not find a ‘hotel’ feel to our venues. Each one is quite different (some are Modern, some Victorian and some are Art-deco era). 

Re Dining: 

Breakfast: We provide a breakfast basket to guests staying in the apartments and cottages. Sadly due to restrictions related to covid, we do not currently offer breakfast in the main house so have reduced prices accordingly and our house-guests enjoy very good breakfasts in one of our many local cafes / restaurants, all within 2-4 minutes of here. (There are three places that we particularly recommend for a great breakfast).   There is however a table set in the bay window and you are welcome to use (Email hidden by Airbnb) plementary Tea, coffee and biscuits are provided in all venues. 

Dinner: There is an excellent choice of restaurants with a variety of cuisines all within walking distance to nearly all of the venues that we offer. 

I'm proud to say that we have won the last 7 awards for 'tourism' and/or 'hospitality' at the Hobsons Bay region Business excellence awards as well as taken out the People's Choice award for the state of Victoria twice in the last three awards. 

Most of our guests are businesspeople or travellers so you can be assured of a quiet, relaxing and private 'home award from home' experience. We want your accommodation to be comfortable and check-ins and check-outs easy so that you can get on with enjoying the reason that you are here.

We look forward to welcoming you to beautiful Williamstown. 

Best regards, 

Melissa and the team from Captains Retreat

Christina

host_about:
We proudly offer you a boutique selection of Rooms, Suites, Apartments and Cottages (many with water views) in beautiful, historic, Williamstown.

Rooms & Suites
Our lovely old home is just one door from the water, boat marina and restaurants and has been tastefully renovated and decorated so that every room has ensuites (some with spas) and most of the rooms also have gas log fires. One of the rooms has its own private lounge and balcony but other guests can enjoy the shared lounge room with fire and bay window.  

Apartments & Cottages
The apartments and cottages that we offer are dotted around Williamstown and most are an easy walk to the restaurants, yacht-clubs and shops. They vary from 1-4 bedrooms and 1-3 bathrooms. (One apartment even has a 4th toilet). 

We are not just offering a spare room in our house. This is our business and we are a dedicated team working to ensure that your stay is comfortable.  We are very careful about the apartments and cottages that we choose to take on and have refused many from owners wanting us to manage them.

Having said that, Williamstown is the oldest suburb in Melbourne and therefore some of the classic older apartments have décor such as shower over the bath. Whilst I would normally say no to venues like this, there are two apartments that have this but their other qualities so far outweigh that one negative and I quietly chip away at the owners in order for that to be changed.  I mention this because we want you to let us know if you have mobility issues so that we can suggest other venues for you. 

Other than beds (which are purchased to order and very comfortable!!), I love to buy antique and pre-loved furniture to fit certain venues and I have them restored using classic and sometimes quirky fabrics so you will not find a ‘hotel’ feel to our venues. Each one is quite different (some are Modern, some Victorian and some are Art-deco era). 

Re Dining: 

Breakfast: We provide a breakfast basket to guests staying in the apartments and cottages. Sadly due to restrictions related to covid, we do not currently offer breakfast in the main house so have reduced prices accordingly and our house-guests enjoy very good breakfasts in one of our many local cafes / restaurants, all within 2-4 minutes of here. (There are three places that we particularly recommend for a great breakfast).   There is however a table set in the bay window and you are welcome to use (Email hidden by Airbnb) plementary Tea, coffee and biscuits are provided in all venues. 

Dinner: There is an excellent choice of restaurants with a variety of cuisines all within walking distance to nearly all of the venues that we offer. 

I'm proud to say that we have won the last 7 awards for 'tourism' and/or 'hospitality' at the Hobsons Bay region Business excellence awards as well as taken out the People's Choice award for the state of Victoria twice in the last three awards. 

Most of our guests are businesspeople or travellers so you can be assured of a quiet, relaxing and private 'home award from home' experience. We want your accommodation to be comfortable and check-ins and check-outs easy so that you can get on with enjoying the reason that you are here.

We look forward to welcoming you to beautiful Williamstown. 

Best regards, 

Melissa and the team from Captains Retreat

host_about:
We proudly offer you a boutique selection of Rooms, Suites, Apartments and Cottages (many with water views) in beautiful, historic, Williamstown.

Rooms & Suites
Our lovely old home is just one door from the water, boat marina and restaurants and has been tastefully renovated and decorated so that every room has ensuites (some with spas) and most of the rooms also have gas log fires. One of the rooms has its own private lounge and balcony but other guests can enjoy the shared lounge room with fire and bay window.  

Apartments & Cottages
The apartments and cottages that we offer are dotted around Williamstown and most are an easy walk to the restaurants, yacht-clubs and shops. They vary from 1-4 bedrooms and 1-3 bathrooms. (One apartment even has a 4th toilet). 

We are not just offering a spare room in our house. This is our business and we are a dedicated team working to ensure that your stay is comfortable.  We are very careful about the apartments and cottages that we choose to take on and have refused many from owners wanting us to manage them.

Having said that, Williamstown is the oldest suburb in Melbourne and therefore some of the classic older apartments have décor such as shower over the bath. Whilst I would normally say no to venues like this, there are two apartments that have this but their other qualities so far outweigh that one negative and I quietly chip away at the owners in order for that to be changed.  I mention this because we want you to let us know if you have mobility issues so that we can suggest other venues for you. 

Other than beds (which are purchased to order and very comfortable!!), I love to buy antique and pre-loved furniture to fit certain venues and I have them restored using classic and sometimes quirky fabrics so you will not find a ‘hotel’ feel to our venues. Each one is quite different (some are Modern, some Victorian and some are Art-deco era). 

Re Dining: 

Breakfast: We provide a breakfast basket to guests staying in the apartments and cottages. Sadly due to restrictions related to covid, we do not currently offer breakfast in the main house so have reduced prices accordingly and our house-guests enjoy very good breakfasts in one of our many local cafes / restaurants, all within 2-4 minutes of here. (There are three places that we particularly recommend for a great breakfast).   There is however a table set in the bay window and you are welcome to use (Email hidden by Airbnb) plementary Tea, coffee and biscuits are provided in all venues. 

Dinner: There is an excellent choice of restaurants with a variety of cuisines all within walking distance to nearly all of the venues that we offer. 

I'm proud to say that we have won the last 7 awards for 'tourism' and/or 'hospitality' at the Hobsons Bay region Business excellence awards as well as taken out the People's Choice award for the state of Victoria twice in the last three awards. 

Most of our guests are businesspeople or travellers so you can be assured of a quiet, relaxing and private 'home award from home' experience. We want your accommodation to be comfortable and check-ins and check-outs easy so that you can get on with enjoying the reason that you are here.

We look forward to welcoming you to beautiful Williamstown. 

Best regards, 

Melissa and the team from Captains Retreat

neighborhood_overview: Williamstown is an historic seaport situated on a small peninsula with delightful views of the city and Port Phillip Bay.
host_about:
We proudly offer you a boutique selection of Rooms, Suites, Apartments and Cottages (many with water views) in beautiful, historic, Williamstown.

Rooms & Suites
Our lovely old home is just one door from the water, boat marina and restaurants and has been tastefully renovated and decorated so that every room has ensuites (some with spas) and most of the rooms also have gas log fires. One of the rooms has its own private lounge and balcony but other guests can enjoy the shared lounge room with fire and bay window.  

Apartments & Cottages
The apartments and cottages that we offer are dotted around Williamstown and most are an easy walk to the restaurants, yacht-clubs and shops. They vary from 1-4 bedrooms and 1-3 bathrooms. (One apartment even has a 4th toilet). 

We are not just offering a spare room in our house. This is our business and we are a dedicated team working to ensure that your stay is comfortable.  We are very careful about the apartments and cottages that we choose to take on and have refused many from owners wanting us to manage them.

Having said that, Williamstown is the oldest suburb in Melbourne and therefore some of the classic older apartments have décor such as shower over the bath. Whilst I would normally say no to venues like this, there are two apartments that have this but their other qualities so far outweigh that one negative and I quietly chip away at the owners in order for that to be changed.  I mention this because we want you to let us know if you have mobility issues so that we can suggest other venues for you. 

Other than beds (which are purchased to order and very comfortable!!), I love to buy antique and pre-loved furniture to fit certain venues and I have them restored using classic and sometimes quirky fabrics so you will not find a ‘hotel’ feel to our venues. Each one is quite different (some are Modern, some Victorian and some are Art-deco era). 

Re Dining: 

Breakfast: We provide a breakfast basket to guests staying in the apartments and cottages. Sadly due to restrictions related to covid, we do not currently offer breakfast in the main house so have reduced prices accordingly and our house-guests enjoy very good breakfasts in one of our many local cafes / restaurants, all within 2-4 minutes of here. (There are three places that we particularly recommend for a great breakfast).   There is however a table set in the bay window and you are welcome to use (Email hidden by Airbnb) plementary Tea, coffee and biscuits are provided in all venues. 

Dinner: There is an excellent choice of restaurants with a variety of cuisines all within walking distance to nearly all of the venues that we offer. 

I'm proud to say that we have won the last 7 awards for 'tourism' and/or 'hospitality' at the Hobsons Bay region Business excellence awards as well as taken out the People's Choice award for the state of Victoria twice in the last three awards. 

Most of our guests are businesspeople or travellers so you can be assured of a quiet, relaxing and private 'home award from home' experience. We want your accommodation to be comfortable and check-ins and check-outs easy so that you can get on with enjoying the reason that you are here.

We look forward to welcoming you to beautiful Williamstown. 

Best regards, 

Melissa and the team from Captains Retreat

description:
Welcome to my CARLISLE PAD!! This apartment is located right in the heart of St Kilda on Carlisle St. The building is NEW and opened late 2018 so it’s very fresh. There’s electronic access to the building and undercover garage so security is great! The apartment is walking distance to all St Kilda has to offer.. Ie: Fitzroy St cafes, bars, shopping & nightlife, Acland St cafes, shops and supermarkets and of course you can walk to THE BEACH! Trams/transport to the city is also at your doorstep.

The space
The apartment is new and fresh. There are two great sized bedrooms, an open living/dining area with a balcony overlooking Carlisle St. The kitchen is filled with everything you need for entertaining and dining and has great new appliances. Don’t want to cook?? No worries....Step out your front door and walk to any of the funky/eclectic cafes on Acland St or Fitzroy St. You will find any cuisine!! The supermarket is within walking distance as is your local tram
neighborhood_overview: My Carlisle Pad is close to everything in the St Kilda area. Stroll down Acland St for eclectic / funky dining or shopping and also check out the nightlife and bar scene in the evenings, bar hopping can be fun and the crowds are fun, flirty and friendly. Fitzroy St has some sophisticated, high end restaurants and Carlisle St in St Kilda East also offers amazing dining, great bars, shopping and cool coffee houses. Supermarkets like Coles & Woolworths are within walking distance as well as the BEACH of course!! The locals are pretty cool and very friendly & St Kilda attracts such a versatile crowd.  I love morning walks/runs along the esplanade and then hitting one of the cafes on Acland St for coffee and an Avocado smash! In the evenings in the Summer there’s nothing better than grabbing some Fish n Chips on Acland St and walking across to sit on the beach to watch the sunset...  ENJOY your time in my Pad!!
host_about:
Hi I’m Mel! I was born in Melbourne and love my city.  These days I live between Melbourne and New York.  My husband and I are very clean, courteous people that believe you need to respect people to be respected.  We love to travel and have visited many wonderful cities in the 20 years we have been together.  My family are my world and we love having fun together.  My life goal is to travel as much as I can, I love making memories.  

Our Elwood Beach House is in a great area of Melbourne.   Elwood Beach is on your front door step and Elwood Village has great cafes, restaurants, boutique shopping and the BEST coffee.  It’s also a hop, skip and a jump to bustling St Kilda and Chapel St.  Public transport is also very handy taking you to Melbourne's CBD, the Arts Centre, Live Theatres and the MCG!  

We have also just listed our new CARLISLE PAD in St Kilda.  Please check it out if you’re after a place to stay right in the heart of St Kilda and don’t need as much space as my Elwood Beach House. It’s perfect for couples or a family who want to explore this fun, vibrant city!

I love hosting people and l always try and make your stay a little special.

I hope you are able to experience the Elwood Beach House or CARLISLE PAD during your stay in Melbourne!!

description:
A simple, earthy offgrid cottage, built with reclaimed timbers and handmade mudbricks.

The Mudbrick Cottage is a peaceful and inviting space where natural living meets beauty. The Cottage has a rustic charm with exposed wood beams, high ceilings, a wood fire, and a newly built deck to enjoy the call of wildlife.

The space
A cosy retreat for nature lovers, couples, bike riders and bush walkers. The property is completely off grid, with power coming from the sun, and water from the rain. If the sun has not been out much, you may hear the hum of the generator powering up the batteries for a short time.

The picturesque town of Warburton has many cafes, specialty stores and walking tracks, it is easy to spend the whole day exploring. The Yarra River snakes through the town centre, and locals can be found swimming and relaxing at the river on hot sunny days.

There are many festivals, markets and sporting events in Warburton, as well as throughout the Yarra Valley. The Valley also has an abundance of wonderful vineyards and renowned restauraunts, perfect for an indulgent weekend.

Warburton is half an hour from Mt Donna Buang. In the winter, the mountain becomes a winter wonderland, where snow play and tobogganing can be enjoyed in the state forest.
host_about: Our family made a tree change to the beautiful Yarra Valley six years ago. Coming home from our busy jobs, we know that as soon as we start driving though the forest down our road we can leave those cares behind and live the simple life. We love walks around the river, the farmer's market in the summer, and a visit up Mount Donna Buang for tobogganing in the winter.

host_about:
Hey there you curious creatures! Time to share a little about ourselves. Mike was born and raised in New Zealand and I have a Greek background but am from a small country town in Victoria. Would you believe that in all the time we’ve been together, I haven’t been able to convince Mike to do the HAKA for me? And if you're wondering, the answer is yes...he’s an ex-rugby player and All Blacks man.

Mike trained as a chef and moved to the UK in his early 20’s to work and travel through Europe. He is a Sensei, 1st Dan black belt and passionate about teaching children the art of Karate. Mike is also a qualified landscaper, is now heavily involved in property and is one of those people who’s annoyingly good at everything.

I graduated and practiced as a Podiatrist for a couple of years, before moving into the advertising industry, security risk management and recently a furniture design & importing business. We launched our hosting journey as a way to help others create unforgettable experiences during their travels whilst having the freedom to personally explore more of our amazing world at the same time!

We’re both fans of entrepreneurship, love Gary Vaynerchuck (if you’ve never heard of him, do yourself a favour and look him up) and enjoy studying personal development, online business, the sharing economy and anything that piques our interest at the time. Podcasts, Kindle, books, online courses...we love learning new things.

Thanks for stopping by. We hope the read was worth it and so look forward connecting with you as hosts or as travellers. We will do our best to make your stay truly memorable in all the right ways and also can’t wait to be great guests if we happen to chance by your Airbnb in your little corner of the globe. 

One more thought to take with you wherever you may be...

We Travel Not To Escape Life, But For Life Not To Escape Us.

See you very soon!


Mike & Panagiota x

neighborhood_overview:
The neighborhood is green and leafy with wide streets, loads of parkland and cute shopping precinct.

Catch the tennis at Melbourne Park. Or hang-out in the CBD, Fitzroy, Collingwood, Abbotsford, Richmond or Hawthorn, all easily accessed by public transport.

The local walking and bike paths are awesome. With frogs, birds, lizards, possums and even the occasional roo, you'd think you were in the bush, not 6km from the city centre.

You can cycle to the city via the Yarra Trail past the Collingwood Children's farm and The Convent, along the Yarra River. The Darebin Creek trail link is close-by and the Merri Creek trail branches-off further afield. All riding can be done on paths, not roads. Otherwise, you can ride the Kew Boulevard, accessed via the main Yarra trail.

host_about:
Hi, my name is Dawei, I started doing Airbnb September 2015. 

I'm a 20 years old undergraduate student currently studying commercial law. I like to watch movies and play video games. Sometimes I could spend my whole day in my room just play games. I thought that there isn't many things to do outside and I thought the World was a boring place. When I'm not playing games, I would read news on the internet just to catch up with the rest of the world. That's how I knew Airbnb. 

My father talked about doing short-term renting. He has got a few new apartments that our relatives bought which needs to be rented out. I told him about Airbnb and he thought we could really make it work. So I asked my best friend if he is interested to be my partner for this, and he said yes. We started almost immediately, planning, buying furniture to started taking guests in just two weeks. 

Then it really changed me.

I met with travelers around the world. Everybody was so polite and friendly.  When I talk to them I can feel the excitement and happiness. It's totally different compared to what I thought people are like. Maybe because this communicate is great, I don't know.  Then I  thought "I want to be people like my guests". I want people around me to feel life is great and there are a lot to look forward to. The guests really gave me a lot of motivation towards my work and my life. Here I have to thank you all.

After one month, the revenue was great, however, take away the interests and loans, all kinds of fees and salary for my partner, there are really not much left for me. But I think that's enough, I'm still a student, I have to spend time on study and don't have many things to spend money on anyway, being able to save money for a holiday with my girlfriend every few months is perfect for me. 

After all these experience, I felt it really changed my life and how I view the world. Doesn't matter if I fail or succeed it's going to affect the rest of my life in a very positive way, that's something really valuable to me.

host_about:
We're Klaudia (Sanctuary Artist), Jonathan (The Oracle), Maria (Fairy Godmother) and Tony (Maker of Worlds), a multi-cultural family all living in Melbourne. We're all different in many ways, but we all share one thing in common: a passion for unique and magical experiences. 

We have long since wished there were easy ways to escape our busy city lives and retreat into a magical, beautiful and peaceful space that feels like another world. This idea eventually evolved into a mission to build with our own hands Melbourne's very own magical sanctuaries and to share it with the rest of the world.

We love imagining what we could create, to build, and to share them with the world through hosting. We constantly think about how to make our creations bring an even greater sense of joy and wonder, and not about how much it'll cost us. We're genuinely excited and happy to host each new guest, to hear about what they love about our creations, and what we could do to make it even better.

We have built and opened our first three installments of Melbourne's hidden sanctuary, which we lovingly refer to as "Heaven & Earth", "Little world of Ice & Snow" and "Mini Renaissance". We have plans to make it even better, as well as other ideas for other worlds we want to try building for our next installments.

We invite you to step into one of our hidden sanctuaries, to follow our journey on social media, and to watch and help us grow by sharing what you think!

neighborhood_overview:

Abbotsford is a dense, inner-city pocket tucked between North Richmond and Clifton Hill, with busy Hoddle Street flanking it on one side, and sprawling green Studley Park calming it down on the other. It’s a characterful mix of terrace houses, warehouse apartments, stylish cafes and the famous Abbotsford Convent arts precinct.

Cycle through Studley Park, buy some produce at the Collingwood Children’s Farm monthly market, drink a cup of famous Melbourne coffee at Three Bags Full or visit any number of cosy pubs in the area.

Elwood, where quaint suburban pockets, heritage homes, vibrant cafes, and wine bars await.

It’s just eight kilometres from Melbourne’s CBD, yet Elwood feels like a town unto itself. Walk east along the canal from Ormond Esplanade on a late afternoon and you’ll notice it feels rather like an island: a small beach suburb in the south of Melbourne that is – by way of culture, community spirit, and public transport – a sea apart from the rest of city.

Like most islands, Elwood has developed its own calm, sophisticated way of life. The people are kind and young, and always outdoors. When you’re out walking the wide avenues, marked with big old plane trees and historic Art Deco homes, you’ll catch smiles from mums with prams, and restaurant owners standing out in the street talking to patrons.

By day, locals and visitors gather at Elwood Beach where the breeze rolls off Port Phillip Bay and cools the neighbouring streets. By night, the town transforms as Ormo

This is the evolution of urban renewal in Melbourne ...... and then .......   watch this space -  Smallfootprint homes and products that reflect our need for simplicity and comfort . Hoping we can welcome you soon .

host_about:
We proudly offer you a boutique selection of Rooms, Suites, Apartments and Cottages (many with water views) in beautiful, historic, Williamstown.

Rooms & Suites
Our lovely old home is just one door from the water, boat marina and restaurants and has been tastefully renovated and decorated so that every room has ensuites (some with spas) and most of the rooms also have gas log fires. One of the rooms has its own private lounge and balcony but other guests can enjoy the shared lounge room with fire and bay window.  

Apartments & Cottages
The apartments and cottages that we offer are dotted around Williamstown and most are an easy walk to the restaurants, yacht-clubs and shops. They vary from 1-4 bedrooms and 1-3 bathrooms. (One apartment even has a 4th toilet). 

We are not just offering a spare room in our house. This is our business and we are a dedicated team working to ensure that your stay is comfortable.  We are very careful about the apartments and cottages that we choose to take on and have refused many from owners wanting us to manage them.

Having said that, Williamstown is the oldest suburb in Melbourne and therefore some of the classic older apartments have décor such as shower over the bath. Whilst I would normally say no to venues like this, there are two apartments that have this but their other qualities so far outweigh that one negative and I quietly chip away at the owners in order for that to be changed.  I mention this because we want you to let us know if you have mobility issues so that we can suggest other venues for you. 

Other than beds (which are purchased to order and very comfortable!!), I love to buy antique and pre-loved furniture to fit certain venues and I have them restored using classic and sometimes quirky fabrics so you will not find a ‘hotel’ feel to our venues. Each one is quite different (some are Modern, some Victorian and some are Art-deco era). 

Re Dining: 

Breakfast: We provide a breakfast basket to guests staying in the apartments and cottages. Sadly due to restrictions related to covid, we do not currently offer breakfast in the main house so have reduced prices accordingly and our house-guests enjoy very good breakfasts in one of our many local cafes / restaurants, all within 2-4 minutes of here. (There are three places that we particularly recommend for a great breakfast).   There is however a table set in the bay window and you are welcome to use (Email hidden by Airbnb) plementary Tea, coffee and biscuits are provided in all venues. 

Dinner: There is an excellent choice of restaurants with a variety of cuisines all within walking distance to nearly all of the venues that we offer. 

I'm proud to say that we have won the last 7 awards for 'tourism' and/or 'hospitality' at the Hobsons Bay region Business excellence awards as well as taken out the People's Choice award for the state of Victoria twice in the last three awards. 

Most of our guests are businesspeople or travellers so you can be assured of a quiet, relaxing and private 'home award from home' experience. We want your accommodation to be comfortable and check-ins and check-outs easy so that you can get on with enjoying the reason that you are here.

We look forward to welcoming you to beautiful Williamstown. 

Best regards, 

Melissa and the team from Captains Retreat
